target.title: fix(ios): native Talk respects session thinking level
target.body:
Closes #111485

AI-assisted: the original patch was prepared with Codex. Maintainer follow-up replaced the source-text assertion with direct request construction coverage and refreshed the branch against current `main`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting native or fallback Talk Mode on iOS could have every spoken turn rejected before model execution when the selected model supported only `off`. The iOS native Talk path hard-coded `thinking: "low"`, overriding the live session and model policy.

Healthy direct OpenAI Realtime WebRTC or gateway-relay sessions do not traverse this native `chat.send` path and are not changed. The fix applies to native Talk and to fallback from unavailable Realtime transport into the native speech pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native Talk now omits the optional `thinking` field from its `chat.send` request. The gateway therefore resolves thinking from the session/model policy, matching the established macOS voice-path behavior.

The request construction is isolated in a narrow internal helper so the iOS app-hosted test can inspect the real `chat.send` parameters rather than scanning Swift source text. The Share Extension and Canvas request paths remain separate and unchanged.

## User Impact

iOS users can use native/fallback Talk with models whose supported thinking catalog contains only `off`. Speech-provider selection remains independent from model thinking policy.

## Evidence

Exact reviewed head: `090bb74b5deeb1b8bf2e402c5a2c2644013e4bda`.

- iPhone 17 Pro simulator, Xcode 27: `TalkModeManagerTests` passed 56/56. The regression constructs the native Talk request and verifies `chat.send`, session/message/idempotency fields, the 30-second run timeout, and absence of `thinking`.
- Actual app UI interaction on the same simulator: `OpenClawSnapshotUITests.testVoiceWakeResumesAfterTalkModeToggle` passed. It launches the app, opens Voice & Talk, toggles Talk Mode on/off, and verifies the app remains healthy.
- Isolated off-only gateway proof on Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01ky41v06mh62f25f81wcgy15s`: the model catalog advertised `thinkingLevels=["off"]`; a request omitting thinking completed with assistant marker `TALK_OFF_ONLY_OK`; exactly one model request was observed. Run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29891564792
- Source-blind behavior validation: pass for native/fallback request shape, off-only compatibility, and healthy direct Realtime exclusion.
- Final branch autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings; patch assessed correct with 0.96 confidence.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

No physical iPhone was connected. Simulator speech capture is intentionally unavailable in the production app, so proof binds the actual app Talk control, the app-hosted native request payload, and the isolated live gateway/model boundary separately rather than claiming a physical spoken recording.
